note: MT reads Geva' (Geba), the town facing Michmash across the gorge; the KJV again substitutes Gibeah.

kjv: so it was a very great trembling
mine: it became a panic from God
note: Hebrew cherdat 'elohim can be a superlative idiom ("a mighty trembling") or literally "a trembling of God"; with the earthquake the narrator likely means a God-sent panic.

kjv: they (the Philistines) went on beating down [one another]
note: Hebrew vayyelekh va-halom is obscure; the KJV derives halom from halam "strike", but it is more likely the adverb "hither", describing the crowd dispersing in all directions.
Hebrew padah normally means "redeem, ransom", implying a payment or substitute for the one under the death oath, not simply a rescue.
Hebrew vayya'as chayil, "he did valour", is an idiom for performing mighty deeds (cf. Num 24:18; Ps 60:12); the KJV takes chayil as "army".
